newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen 96 metals futures turnover falls 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen 96 metals futures turnover falls 30 pct.

text.p: Turnover on the Shenzhen Non-ferrous Metals Futures Exchange fell sharply in 1996 after authorities tightened controls over speculation in commodities futures markets, an exchange official said on Monday.
Turnover in 1996 was 147.59 billion yuan, down more than 30 percent from 1995, the official said.
The exchange stepped up risk control in 1996 to comply with anti-speculation drives by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the country's top securities watchdog, he said.
Control policies aimed at preventing the flow of state assets into markets include the restriction of speculative activities by state enterprises and state financial institutions.
The official said the exchange would focus on bringing its futures operations in line with international standards in the run-up to Hong Kong's handover to Chinese rule on July 1.
He declined to give further details.
